newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in very quiet trade on Monday, with many players sidelined ahead of the week's economic reports and amid speculation about an interest rate hike, dealers said.

"It's just more of a continuation of a buyers strike from last week," said a dealer at a Canadian bank. "In essence everybody is sitting on the sidelines. You've got a lot of economic data coming down this week and you've got foreign exchange traders putting pressure on the Bank of Canada."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded with a yield of 3.40 percent, unchanged from Friday's close.
Key economic releases out this week include real Canadian and U.S. gross domestic product data out on Thursday and U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday.

In the interim, many dealers are closely watching the currency, with expectations that further weakness could prompt the Bank of Canada to hike rates. The central bank last hiked rates on June 26, partly to offset a weaker dollar. T-bill dealers said currency traders were pushing the bank for a tightening although inflation remained subdued.
"I call it terrorism more than anything else," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.81 percent from 3.78 percent at Friday's close. The one-year when-issued T-bill softened to yield 4.31 percent from 4.30 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.25 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
